dedupe_keys.name: climate shelters as an urban network for climate resilience in naples secap and bagnoli design case

description: This case study applies a method for identifying and designing climate shelters, permanent urban spaces that reduce heatwave effects while delivering social, energy and environmental co-benefits, to the city of Naples, Italy. It is reported by Giovanni Nocerino, Maria Teresa Girardi and Mattia Federico Leone in the journal TECHNE (Firenze University Press), published on 29 July 2026. The framework combines technical, environmental and functional indicators with GIS and algorithm-aided design to turn existing spaces into resilience and neighbourhood service nodes. At city scale it is linked to Naples' Sustainable Energy and Climate Action Plan, showing how a network of shelters can reduce energy poverty and serve vulnerable residents; at site scale the Bagnoli district is used to turn these strategic goals into design proposals. Coverage is the city of Naples with a detailed design in Bagnoli. Access: open-access article online. Licence: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0; free. Caveats: a planning and design study; built outcomes and measured cooling are not reported in the abstract. Simulation uses: indicator-based siting of cooling refuges, and a reference for heat-adaptation scenarios in public space. Related records: the Miami-Dade tree canopy statistics and 3-30-300 greening datasets.
name: Climate shelters as an urban network for climate resilience in Naples (SECAP and Bagnoli design case)
outcomes: The method identified public spaces in Naples that can serve as permanent climate shelters, linked them to the city's climate action plan as a network that also addresses energy poverty, and produced a concrete shelter design for Bagnoli.
provider: TECHNE Journal of Technology for Architecture and Environment (Firenze University Press)
